session_cue.text: Drop Dead Ned's blood-red wasp spinning inside Sir Alfred's ribs

previous.text: Drop Dead Ned's wasp broke apart the undead knight Sir Alfred, and the party left him incapacitated but not destroyed.
Dr. Uriah's new spell located the dragon's lair on the treasure map. The witch Vivian advised drugging the dragon with faun wine.
Wayman persuaded the goblins to wall off the mound's upper rooms and destroy its church. The party later trailed drunk goblins to King Hogboon's temple castle.
Dr. Uriah kept the barrow robes after a deal with Brother Dirk, then found they are not magical.
Sir Phidipaldi and Dr. Uriah realized their treasure map came from the dwarf Bral. The map also marks the Dwarven mine.
Sir Phidipaldi persuaded Warwick the smith to lend the party his grandfather's mithril chain shirt.
Cedric and Warwick described their lost supplies, and Warwick pointed the party to a mine in the north.
At Sir Phidipaldi's insistence, Cedric signed a promissory note for the party's barrow treasure.
The party recruited Lady Hilda and the wizard Malzazarik using Cedric's promissory note.
Dunk put on a magic ring from a dead dwarf in the cave-in and met Grimny's ghost.
Grimny's ghost told Dunk he believes his greedy brother Bral murdered him.

current.where_you_are: The party stands at the caved-in entrance of the Dwarven mine, beside the burnt cabin at the base of the hill. Malzazarik the Magnificent and Lady Hilda are with them.

Your goals.text: Kill the black dragon and drag its body into Brandonsford to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold.
Find the treasure marked on the party's treasure map.
Fight Eric the Reeve in the dawn duel Sir Phidipaldi challenged him to.
Get Farmer Gill's mule Shamus. Gill asked 100 gold but says he may go lower.

Standing in your way.text: A cave-in seals the Dwarven mine's old entrance, blocking the metal owed to Warwick. It looks natural and can be dug through.
George says arrows and swords failed against the dragon's black scales, and it has a deadly poison bite and spits sulfur. Father William says only Sir Brandon's sword can kill it.
The dragon reported in the Dragon's Lair stands between the party and the hoard there. Dunk suspects there is no dragon, only Bral pretending.
Farmer Gill won't lower his price for Shamus until his boys return, since he can't work without them or a mule.
Farmer Gill says Warwick always refuses to sell the mithril chain shirt he displays.

What could help.text: The treasure map marks the Dragon's Lair. George places it at the foot of the northern mountains, and Grimny says it is one big room.
Sir Phidipaldi carries Sir Brandon's magic sword, which killed the first dragon and is far more effective against evil beings.
The party has enough faun wine. Vivian says enough of it would knock out the dragon so they could drive the sword through its mouth.
Sir Phidipaldi proposes that if the party leaves game dosed with faun wine outside the dragon's cave, they can go in once the dragon eats it.
Lady Hilda and the wizard Malzazarik have joined the party.
Wayman wears Warwick's mithril chain shirt on loan. It greatly improves his protection and halves damage from magic weapons and spells.
Grimny's ghost says Bral probably hid the dwarves' hoard in the Dragon's Lair.
Cedric signed a promissory note for the barrow treasure, worth 975 gold by Dr. Uriah's tally, payable once the caravans flow again.
The borrowed mithril shirt could protect Wayman against the dragon.
Drop Dead Ned travels with the party as a hired scout for a 100 gold fee, carrying tools such as a crowbar.
The party holds a treasure map of sites near Brandonsford, with one marked location still unidentified.
The Barrow Mound mosaics show Sir Brandon killed the first dragon by driving his sword up through its open mouth.
Squints the halfling has joined the party as Trout's junior assistant, taking orders from Trout.

Still unanswered.text: How did Grimny die, and did his brother Bral kill him?
How did Sir Brandon really kill the first dragon?
What happened to Grimny's brothers Grelli, Durney, Brenny, Tedry and Rooney?
Where has this new dragon come from?
What is stopping shipments into Brandonsford, including Bentley's overdue restock?
Whose female voice asked "What makes a true knight?" in the tomb?
Why are the once-hidden fairies now coming out more often?

Promises and debts.text: The party must bring Warwick metal from the Dwarven mine in exchange for the mithril shirt loan. Meanwhile he plays Sir Phidipaldi's lyre each night.
Dr. Uriah owes Father William penance at the Barrow Mound and a 10 gold donation for its upkeep.
The party owes Lady Hilda and Malzazarik pay for joining, pledged against Cedric's 975-gold promissory note.
The party must return the mithril chain shirt Warwick lent them. Warwick holds Sir Phidipaldi's plate armor and lyre as collateral.
Trout must let Squints pick from the Halfling Corps' first treasure after the elite members. Until then Squints pays his own way.
Dr. Uriah must return the barrow robes to the church once the dragon is defeated, as he promised Brother Dirk.
Sir Phidipaldi vowed to George to bring his lance against the dragon.

Meanwhile.text: The black dragon that tore off George's arm is still at large around Brandonsford and may maim others.
George says the dragon can't fly yet but soon will, and then they are doomed.
A slow, man-eating giant in a cyclopean cottage north of Brandonsford is now awake. He chased the party until he tired.

threads.name: The treasure map
threads.note: The map's origin is answered (won from Bral, beat_72), two locations are read, and Grimny says the hoard is probably in the Dragon's Lair (beat_74). The treasure is still unrecovered and one location is unidentified.

threads.name: The Clurichen of the riverbanks
threads.note: Not touched this Session; Sir Phidipaldi's Clurichen story to Warwick does not bear on Naggeneen.

threads.name: The dragon and the Reeve's bounty

threads.name: Hiring Lady Hilda
threads.note: Lady Hilda and the wizard Malzazarik joined the party, recruited against Cedric's promissory note rather than a Reeve advance (beat_61). Their pay under that arrangement remains open.

threads.name: Drop Dead Ned's offer
threads.note: Ned's wasp incapacitated Sir Alfred. Ned remains with the party and his offers still stand.

threads.name: Brandonsford's missing shipments
threads.note: Cedric and Warwick say supplies stopped when the dragon troubles began (beat_25, beat_28), which partly answers why shipments stopped.

threads.name: Sir Phidipaldi's quarrel with Eric the Reeve
threads.note: Not touched this Session.

threads.name: Shamus the mule
threads.note: Not touched this Session.

threads.name: Warwick's mithril chain shirt
threads.note: Warwick lent the mithril shirt, holding the plate armor and lyre as collateral, in exchange for metal from the Dwarven mine (beat_34, beat_35). That metal is still owed.

threads.name: Squints and Trout's Halfling Corps
threads.note: Not touched this Session.

threads.name: Ingrid's sleeping potion for Warwick
threads.note: Sir Phidipaldi told Ingrid that Warwick knows of her visits and is not interested (beat_57), and the shirt was obtained another way. Dunk's promise to Ingrid was never released, so the thread stays open.

threads.name: Dr. Uriah's penance and donation at the Barrow Mound
threads.note: Not touched this Session.

threads.name: Why the hidden fairies are coming out
threads.note: Not touched; fairy magic in the forest was only colour.

threads.name: The giant in the cyclopean cottage
threads.note: Not touched this Session.

threads.name: The undead swordsman of the Barrow Mound
threads.note: The swordsman is identified as the undead knight Sir Alfred, and he was incapacitated but not destroyed (beat_9). The danger remains.

threads.name: The Free Goblin Society's bargain
threads.note: The deal was renegotiated: the goblins stay, wall off the stairs and keep the upper rooms (beat_13), and Wayman renewed the promise not to tell King Hogboon (beat_15). That promise remains owed.

threads.name: Brother Dirk and the Barrow's holy relics
threads.note: The robes proved non-magical (beat_40), and Dr. Uriah promised to return them to the church after the dragon is defeated (beat_24). The chalice question is still open.

threads.name: The noblewoman statue and the voice in the tomb
threads.note: Not touched this Session.

threads.name: Cedric's promissory note
threads.note: Cedric signed a note for the barrow treasure, tallied at 975 gold, payable once the caravans flow. It is unpaid and has been pledged to recruit allies.

threads.name: Vivian's message to Grimny
threads.note: The party agreed to carry Vivian's letter and scent to Grimny. Dunk delivered both to Grimny's ghost, who ascended (beat_78), so nothing remains owed.

threads.name: Dunk's dwarven ring
threads.note: Dunk wears a magical ring taken from a dead dwarf that let him see Grimny's ghost. Whether it is cursed is unknown.

threads.name: Bral and Grimny's murder
threads.note: Grimny believes his brother Bral killed him, and Bral's whereabouts and the fate of the other dwarves are unknown. Dunk suspects Bral may be faking the dragon.

facts.text: Find the treasure marked on the party's treasure map.
The party holds a treasure map marking several locations near Brandonsford; one marked location is still unidentified.

classification.support_basis: The map marks where the treasure and related sites lie, guiding the party toward the hoard.

facts.text: Where is the treasure the map marks?
facts.ended_how: replaced by fact_new_1: Grimny says the hoard is probably in the Dragon's Lair

classification.grounding_justification: The map conspicuously marks treasure without saying where.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Settled by identifying a location.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly instrumental to finding the treasure.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Supported reading the map and questioning sources.

facts.text: The party plans to check one of the map's marked locations on its way north through the forest.
facts.ended_how: used up: the party went to the Dwarven mine, a marked location

classification.support_basis: Visiting a marked location could reveal treasure or clues to it.
classification.action_basis: The party was travelling north past marked locations.

facts.text: Where did the party's treasure map come from?
facts.ended_how: answered: the map came from Bral, who lost it to the party in a bet

classification.grounding_justification: The map's provenance was raised as unresolved.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Its answer revealed a relationship to the dwarves and Bral.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Linking the map to Bral changed the party's understanding.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Supported following leads to its maker.

facts.text: Grimny's ghost said Bral probably hid the dwarves' hoard in the Dragon's Lair, a cave the dwarves had scouted as a hiding spot nobody would ever go.

classification.support_basis: It points the party to the hoard's likely location, though Grimny only says 'probably'.

facts.resource_subject: Where the dwarves' hoard probably is (hidden by Bral in the Dragon's Lair)

facts.text: Dr. Uriah's Read Languages spell lets him read the writing under one location on the treasure map per day.

classification.support_basis: It can identify the map's remaining unlabelled location.

facts.text: What is the treasure map's remaining unidentified location? Sir Phidipaldi guesses it is King Hogboon's.

classification.grounding_justification: Play explicitly notes one marked location remains unidentified.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A single reading of the label would settle it.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mostly instrumental identification.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: An available spell answers it directly.

facts.text: The dragon reported in the Dragon's Lair stands between the party and the hoard hidden there.
facts.uncertain_reason: Dunk speculates there is no dragon, only Bral pretending there is one.

classification.scope_basis: The dragon is an ongoing regional danger the party must face to enter the lair.

facts.text: Naggeneen, held in a bag behind Quinn's bar at the Golden Egg, offers his pot of gold or a secret to whoever lets him go.

classification.support_basis: No established want or debt of the party is served by Naggeneen's gold or secret.
classification.action_basis: Naggeneen offered his gold or a secret for release, but no want or debt it would advance is established.

facts.text: What does Quinn intend to do with the captive Naggeneen?

classification.grounding_justification: A captive fairy held in a bag behind a bar raises the question of the captor's purpose.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal Quinn's intention, an underlying motive.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mildly interesting, but mainly explains a side situation.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be learned by questioning Quinn or observing the bar, little more.

facts.text: Kill the black dragon troubling Brandonsford and drag its body into town to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold.
Lady Hilda would join the party against the dragon for pay (see her offer's thread).
facts.ended_how: used up: Lady Hilda joined the party, recruited with Cedric's promissory note

classification.support_basis: A noble warrior adds fighting strength against the dragon.
classification.action_basis: Lady Hilda offered to join for pay.

facts.text: Where has this new dragon come from, centuries after Sir Brandon killed the first?

classification.grounding_justification: A dragon reappearing centuries after the first was slain is a conspicuous anomaly.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal a hidden cause behind the dragon's appearance.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Its origin would explain the town's troubles.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Lair, church lore and local witnesses could all be followed.

facts.text: The black dragon, which tore off George the woodsman's arm, is still at large around Brandonsford and may maim others.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Maiming or killing of locals is a specific harm.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: George's lost arm is direct evidence of the dragon's attacks.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Its attacks and the halted shipments show an ongoing pattern.
classification.preventability_justification: The party is preparing to kill it and knows where its lair is.

facts.text: Farmer Gill's three sons are hunting the dragon now and could kill it before the party, taking the Reeve's bounty.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Losing the bounty to rivals is specific.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Loss of a reward, not physical harm.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: They are reported to be hunting it, but weapons have failed against it.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Nothing new shows them nearing success.
classification.preventability_justification: The party can hurry to the lair first.

facts.text: The treasure map marks the Dragon's Lair, which George says is up north at the foot of the mountains with no climbing needed; Grimny says the dwarves once scouted it as a very small cave with just one big room.

classification.support_basis: A marked location and known one-room layout let the party find and plan its approach to the dragon.

facts.resource_subject: The Dragon's Lair's map location and layout (small cave, one big room)

facts.text: Nothing pierces the dragon's black scales: George says his friends' arrows and swords all failed, and Father William says it can't be killed without the magic sword buried with Sir Brandon. Its jaws drip poison whose bite kills, and it spits sulfur.

classification.scope_basis: The dragon's armor and poison are inherent and remain whenever the party confronts it; no remedy for the poison was found this Session.

facts.text: Wayman now wears Warwick's borrowed mithril chain shirt, which could protect him against the dragon (see its thread).

classification.support_basis: The shirt greatly improves Wayman's protection in a fight with the dragon; whether it helps against poison is not established.

facts.resource_subject: The mithril shirt on loan, worn by Wayman

facts.text: George says the dragon can't fly yet but soon will, and then they are doomed.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: A flying dragon would be far harder to stop and could range widely, though 'doomed' is vague.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: A flying dragon would endanger the whole region.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: George describes it as growing toward flight, but no timeline.
classification.preventability_justification: Killing it soon would prevent it.

facts.text: Does Eric the Reeve actually have the 1000 gold he promised for the dragon?

classification.grounding_justification: Doubt was raised earlier, and Sir Phidipaldi still worries the Reeve won't pay in advance.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A single fact about the Reeve's funds.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly practical.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be checked by asking around or confronting the Reeve.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi vowed to George to bring his lance against the dragon, which George allows may be one of the few weapons not yet tried.

classification.stake_basis: George only allowed the lance might work; he wants the dragon dead, not the lance specifically used.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi carries Sir Brandon's magical sword, the blade that killed the first dragon: silvery white, not cursed, etched "All shadows yield to my light", and far more effective against evil beings.

classification.support_basis: Father William says the dragon can't be killed without this sword, so it may overcome its impenetrable scales; whether the dragon counts as evil is not established.

facts.resource_subject: Sir Brandon's sword is far more effective against evil beings

facts.text: The Barrow Mound mosaics show Sir Brandon slew the first dragon by driving his sword up through the roof of its open mouth.

classification.support_basis: It suggests a way past the scales, though Vivian notes the tale comes only from Sir Brandon himself and reaching a moving dragon's mouth is hard.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi plans to stop at the witch's place or the alchemist for protection against the black dragon's poison.
facts.ended_how: used up: the party consulted both Ingrid and the witch Vivian, and neither has a remedy for the dragon's poison

classification.support_basis: A poison remedy would reduce the risk of the dragon's lethal bite.
classification.action_basis: The witch and alchemist were local and accessible.

facts.text: The party has enough faun wine; Vivian says a sufficient amount, if the dragon drank it, would knock it out so they could drive the sword through its mouth as Sir Brandon did.

classification.support_basis: Knocking the dragon out would solve the problem of reaching its moving mouth, though it rests on Vivian's word and the dragon must drink it.

facts.resource_subject: The party's supply of faun wine

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi plans to dose caught game with faun wine and leave it outside the dragon's cave, then go in once the dragon has eaten it.

classification.support_basis: Baited game is a way to get the dragon to drink the wine and be knocked out before the party enters.
classification.action_basis: The party holds enough faun wine, knows where the lair is and can hunt game.

facts.text: How did Sir Brandon really kill the first dragon?

classification.grounding_justification: Vivian explicitly says it is hard to know, since he had many companions but only he told the tale.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: It would reveal a hidden historical truth behind the legend.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Could reinterpret the town's founding legend.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Vivian says the church knows the tale; records and the barrow could be examined.

facts.text: Is there really a dragon, or is Bral faking one to keep everybody away from the lair?

classification.grounding_justification: Only Dunk's speculation, prompted by Grimny saying Bral likely hid the hoard in the then-empty cave; George's lost arm argues against it.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A yes would expose a concealed scheme linking the dragon, the hoard and Grimny's murder.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: A fake dragon would be a major reinterpretation.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Visiting the lair would largely settle it.

facts.text: Lady Hilda, a seasoned fighter in chain mail with a shield, offers to join the party against the dragon for pay.
facts.ended_how: used up: Lady Hilda joined the party, recruited against Cedric's promissory note (beat_61)

classification.support_basis: A seasoned armored fighter adds substantial fighting strength for the dragon hunt.
classification.action_basis: Lady Hilda offered her services for pay.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi told Lady Hilda the party would talk to the Reeve and then come back to take up her services.
facts.ended_how: fulfilled in substance: the party came back and took up her services, using Cedric's note instead of the Reeve (beat_61)

classification.stake_basis: Hilda wanted to be hired; no evidence she relied on the Reeve conversation itself.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi plans to use Sir Brandon's sword as proof of competence to strong-arm the reeve into an advance, then use the advance to pay Lady Hilda and henchmen.
facts.ended_how: obsolete: the party recruited Lady Hilda and Malzazarik against Cedric's promissory note instead of a Reeve advance (beat_29, beat_61)

classification.support_basis: An advance would have funded hiring Lady Hilda; Phidipaldi doubted the Reeve would pay in advance.
classification.action_basis: The plan relied on the Reeve agreeing, which was never established.

facts.text: The party owes Lady Hilda and the wizard Malzazarik pay for joining, pledged against Cedric's 975-gold promissory note for the party's treasure.
facts.uncertain_reason: Play never stated how much each is owed or exactly how the note pays them.

classification.stake_basis: Hilda offered her services for pay and both joined on the strength of the note, so they rely on being paid.

facts.text: Lady Hilda, a seasoned fighter in chain mail with a shield, and the wizard Malzazarik have joined the party.

classification.support_basis: An armored fighter and a wizard substantially add to the party's strength for the dragon hunt.

facts.text: Drop Dead Ned, a killer with a little killer wasp, is hired by the party for a 100 gold fee and travels with them, scouting ahead and carrying tools such as a crowbar.

classification.support_basis: Ned is a hired combatant and scout whose wasp just incapacitated the undead knight Sir Alfred, a capability that could help against the dragon hunt's dangers, though no use against the dragon itself is established.

facts.text: Ned pays the party 10 gold back each time they let him murder somebody, provided he may do whatever he wants with the body.

classification.support_basis: It yields small rebates of gold, but play establishes no want or debt the money serves.
classification.action_basis: Ned himself offered the rebate on these terms; the party need only let him kill someone and keep the body.

facts.text: Ned offers to buy the bodies of the dead goblins in the Barrow Mound's lower corridor for 5 gold each.
facts.possibly_moot: The party left the Barrow Mound (beat_9, beat_16) and the goblins are settling there and walling off the stairs (beat_13); Ned never withdrew the offer.

classification.support_basis: It would yield a few gold, but play establishes no want or debt the money serves.
classification.action_basis: Ned offered the price himself; the party would have to retrieve the bodies from the barrow.

facts.text: The Free Goblin Society would not want their dead compatriots defiled, so the party would have to sneak the goblin bodies past them to sell them to Ned.

classification.scope_basis: The goblins now remain living at the Barrow Mound (beat_13), so their objection persists beyond any one scene.

facts.text: Cedric and Warwick say shipments into Brandonsford stopped when the dragon troubles began; what exactly is stopping them, including Bentley's overdue restock?

classification.grounding_justification: Two townsfolk tie the halt to the dragon's arrival, but nobody says how the dragon stops caravans, leaving the mechanism conspicuously open.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal the underlying circumstance cutting off the town, possibly connected to the dragon's true nature.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Knowing what really halts the caravans would change the party's understanding of the town's plight.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: It can be pursued by questioning merchants or tracing the caravan route.

facts.text: Cedric and Warwick say supplies have not reached Brandonsford since the dragon appeared; until the caravans flow again, Cedric cannot pay out his promissory note for the party's treasure.

classification.scope_basis: The supply halt has lasted weeks to months and Cedric's payment is explicitly conditioned on caravans flowing again, so it persists beyond the store scene.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi wants to fight Eric the Reeve in the duel he challenged him to at dawn.
Will Eric the Reeve, offended by Sir Phidipaldi, accept his challenge to a duel at dawn?

classification.grounding_justification: A prior Session established the challenge and Eric's offence, leaving his acceptance unresolved.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A simple yes-or-no about Eric's response, settled by asking him.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mildly interesting for the quarrel but mainly a bounded outcome.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Answered by confronting Eric directly; little to investigate.

facts.text: Get Farmer Gill's mule Shamus; Gill asked 100 gold but says he is willing to go lower.
When Dunk asked to trade work for Shamus, Farmer Gill said the big work needed is killing the dragon; he did not say outright he would give the mule for it.

classification.support_basis: Killing the dragon might earn Gill's goodwill toward giving or discounting Shamus, but Gill never agreed to that trade.
classification.action_basis: Gill only named the dragon as the big work needed; he did not offer the mule in exchange, so the trade itself is not established.

facts.text: Farmer Gill can get no work done without his boys or a mule, so he won't drop his price for Shamus until his boys come back.

classification.scope_basis: Gill's stated refusal lasts until his boys return, a standing condition beyond any one scene.

facts.text: Acquire the mithril chain shirt Warwick the smith displays in his shop.
facts.possibly_moot: Warwick lent the shirt to the party (beat_35), so the party now holds it on loan but does not own it.

facts.text: Farmer Gill says Warwick always refuses to sell the mithril chain shirt he displays.

classification.scope_basis: Warwick only lent the shirt and never agreed to sell it; it is his grandfather's armor (beat_58), so the refusal still stands against owning it.

facts.text: Dunk says Warwick's mithril chain shirt is magical armor that could help against the dragon, once the party has it.

classification.support_basis: Magical armor would protect a fighter against the dragon.
classification.action_basis: The party needed to obtain the shirt first.

facts.text: Dunk's plan to help Ingrid get her sleeping potion to Warwick could let him into Warwick's house to take the shirt.
facts.ended_how: obsolete: Warwick lent the party the shirt (beat_35), and Ingrid has been told Warwick knows of her visits (beat_57)

classification.support_basis: It would have given access to the shirt.
classification.action_basis: Plan to help Ingrid deliver her potion.

facts.text: What magic does Warwick's mithril chain shirt hold?
facts.ended_how: answered: it greatly improves protection and halves damage from magic weapons and spells (beat_36)

classification.grounding_justification: The shirt was said to be magical without its effect being known.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A simple property of an item.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly instrumental information.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Settled by wearing or testing it.

facts.text: The party must bring Warwick metal from the Dwarven mine, in exchange for his loan of the mithril chain shirt; meanwhile Warwick keeps Sir Phidipaldi's lyre to play each night.

classification.stake_basis: Warwick says he is out of metal and cannot make a living, and he asked for this metal specifically in exchange for the loan.

facts.text: The party must return the mithril chain shirt Warwick lent them; Warwick holds Sir Phidipaldi's plate armor and lyre as collateral.

classification.stake_basis: The shirt was Warwick's grandfather's armor, which he never let Ingrid touch, and he demanded collateral for it.

facts.text: Wayman wears Warwick's mithril chain shirt, on loan; it greatly improves his protection and halves damage from magic weapons and spells.

classification.support_basis: Sir Phidipaldi asked for the shirt so the party would not get killed in the Dwarven mine, and its protection makes the trip to fetch Warwick's metal safer.

facts.resource_subject: The mithril shirt on loan, worn by Wayman

facts.text: A cave-in seals the Dwarven mine's old entrance, north of town and marked on the treasure map, blocking the party from the metal owed to Warwick; it looks natural and can be dug through.

classification.scope_basis: The cave-in is a physical seal on the mine entrance that remains until dug through; Dunk only partly cleared it.

facts.text: Does the Dwarven mine still hold metal for Warwick?

classification.grounding_justification: Little is known of the mine beyond Warwick's belief that there is metal there, and Grimny says the dwarves' good stuff went into a hoard.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A bounded fact settled by getting inside the mine.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly instrumental for the debt.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Settled by digging through and looking.

facts.text: Under Trout's recruitment terms, once the Halfling Corps finds its first treasure Squints gets to pick from it after the elite members; until then Squints funds himself and his gear and takes orders from Trout.

classification.stake_basis: Squints joined and funds himself on the understanding that he will get a pick of the Corps' first treasure.

facts.text: Squints, a halfling more experienced at fighting than Trout and armed with a sling and dagger, has joined the party as Trout's junior assistant and takes orders directly from Trout.

classification.support_basis: An extra armed fighter adds a small amount of combat strength to the party's dangerous ventures such as the dragon hunt.

facts.text: Trout, with Phidipaldi's agreement, secretly intends not to rescue Squints if he is caught while sent into danger, despite promising him intervention.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: The specific harm is Squints being left captured or in danger without the promised rescue.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Serious harm or capture of one companion.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: The intent was stated by Trout and agreed by Phidipaldi.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: No situation sending Squints into danger has yet arisen.
classification.preventability_justification: The party controls whether to send Squints into danger and whether to rescue him.

facts.text: Dunk owes Ingrid help getting into Warwick's house and giving Warwick her sleeping potion, so she can watch him sleep without fear of waking him, in exchange for her making the potion.
facts.possibly_moot: Sir Phidipaldi told Ingrid that Warwick knows of her visits and is not interested (beat_57), she left crestfallen (beat_59), and the party got the mithril shirt by loan instead (beat_35); Ingrid never released Dunk.

classification.stake_basis: Ingrid made the potion in exchange specifically so she could watch Warwick sleep undisturbed, though Warwick's knowledge of her visits may have removed her interest.

facts.text: Ingrid is making a sleeping potion from the faun wine Dunk gave her; Dunk can collect it when they meet tonight and use it to put Warwick to sleep.
facts.possibly_moot: The mithril shirt was lent to the party (beat_35) and Ingrid was told Warwick knows of her visits and is not interested (beat_57), removing the potion's apparent purpose.
facts.uncertain_reason: No beat shows whether Dunk met Ingrid or collected the potion, or whether she still means to hand it over.

classification.support_basis: The potion is what Dunk owes to give Warwick under his bargain with Ingrid, though its potency is in doubt.
classification.action_basis: Ingrid agreed to make the potion for Dunk to collect.

facts.text: Warwick sleeps in a second-story bedroom above his shop whose window is left cracked open; Ingrid climbs up to it every night.

classification.support_basis: The open window is a way into Warwick's house, needed to give him the potion under Dunk's bargain.
classification.action_basis: The window is physically open and Ingrid already climbs to it nightly.

facts.text: Dunk knows Ingrid secretly watches Warwick sleep every night, which she dreads him learning, and he has hinted he might not keep it secret.
facts.ended_how: obsolete: Sir Phidipaldi told Ingrid that Warwick already knows of her visits (beat_57), so the secret is no longer leverage

classification.support_basis: The secret gave Dunk leverage over Ingrid.

facts.text: The fauns of the Faun Grove trade their faun wine for sentimental items such as a love letter or a pixie's treasure.
facts.ended_how: no longer relevant: the party has enough faun wine and need not return to the fauns (beat_62)

classification.support_basis: More faun wine could have strengthened the sleeping potion.
classification.action_basis: The fauns trade wine for sentimental items.

facts.text: Will a potion made from Dunk's heavily diluted faun wine still put Warwick to sleep?

classification.grounding_justification: Earlier play established the wine was heavily diluted, raising doubt about potency.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A single test would settle it.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Purely instrumental information.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Settled by trying the potion.

facts.text: Does Ingrid really make her potions herself, as she claims, or can't she, as Father William says?

classification.grounding_justification: Conflicting claims from Ingrid and Father William, plus Vivian's admission that she only tells Ingrid which herbs to find, make it a live contradiction.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer reveals a hidden circumstance about Ingrid's craft.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mildly interesting about Ingrid, mainly bearing on potion reliability.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be checked by questioning Ingrid or Vivian or watching her work.

facts.text: Dr. Uriah owes Father William penance at the Barrow Mound and a 10 gold donation for the Mound's upkeep.

classification.stake_basis: Father William assigned the penance and asked for the donation specifically for the Mound's upkeep, so the church relies on this payment and penance.

facts.text: Why are fairies that used to stay hidden now encroaching and coming out more often, as Ingrid reports?

classification.grounding_justification: Ingrid reported a change in fairy behaviour, an anomaly that clearly raises the question.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal an underlying cause behind a change in the fairies' behaviour.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Explaining why hidden fairies emerge could reveal a hidden development in the region, though it is not yet tied to other events.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be pursued through Ingrid, Vivian or the fairy-touched forest, plausibly supporting leads.

facts.text: A slow-moving giant living in an oversized cottage of cyclopean rocks in the woods north of Brandonsford captures people to eat; Brother Dirk says the giant meant to cook him in a stew. The giant is now awake and chased the party until he tired.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Being captured and eaten is a specific identified harm.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Brother Dirk's testimony and the party being chased support it.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: The giant is awake and has already captured someone and chased the party.
classification.preventability_justification: The giant is slow and tires, so the party can avoid his cottage or outrun him.

facts.text: The undead knight Sir Alfred, a seven-foot skeleton with a huge greatsword, lies incapacitated but not destroyed in the Barrow Mound; the goblins say he killed many of their kin below.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: If he recovers he could again kill those in the mound, as he killed many goblins and nearly hit Dunk.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: He has killed many goblins; a renewed attack could be deadly.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: He was directly observed attacking and is known to be only incapacitated, not destroyed.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Nothing shows he is recovering or will rise again; it is only possible.
classification.preventability_justification: The party could return and destroy him, with Sir Brandon's sword known to be effective against him, though Brother Dirk prefers he be spared.

facts.text: Who is the undead swordsman? Is it one of Sir Brandon's companions from the mosaics?
facts.ended_how: answered: he is the undead knight Sir Alfred

classification.grounding_justification: An unidentified undead knight appeared in Sir Brandon's tomb, near mosaics of his companions.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Mainly an identification.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Linking him to Sir Brandon's companions would be mildly interesting.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Little beyond identifying him.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi promised the Free Goblin Society that the party would clear the evil from the Barrow Mound so the goblins can live there free from King Hogboon. In exchange the goblins walk with the party and gift him his 'father's goods'.
facts.ended_how: released: the goblins accepted a renegotiated deal to stay, wall off the stairs and keep the upper rooms instead (beat_13)

classification.stake_basis: The goblins wanted the mound cleared so they could live there free from King Hogboon; Sir Alfred had killed their friends below.

facts.text: Wayman promised Snurk of the Free Goblin Society that he will never tell King Hogboon where the goblins are, now that they live in the Barrow Mound's upper rooms.

classification.stake_basis: The goblins fled King Hogboon and considered having to go back and beg his forgiveness, so their safety depends on him not learning where they are.

facts.text: The undead greatsword-wielder who has been killing goblins below blocks clearing the evil from the Barrow Mound.
facts.ended_how: obsolete: the clearing promise was replaced by the renegotiated deal, and Sir Alfred was left incapacitated (see thread_17)

classification.scope_basis: The undead knight had killed goblins below over time, blocking the mound's clearing beyond one scene.

facts.text: What is making the scratching sounds at the far west end of the Barrow Mound's lower corridor?
facts.ended_how: obsolete: the episode that made it matter has ended; the party left the mound and the goblins are walling off the lower level

classification.grounding_justification: Unexplained sounds were noted in the lower corridor.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: One look would likely settle what makes the noise.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly a local curiosity.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Little beyond going to look.

facts.text: Do the robes of Saint Arthur, now worn by Dr. Uriah, hold any magic?
facts.ended_how: answered: witch powder showed the robes are not magical, just a religious relic

classification.grounding_justification: The robes came from a holy tomb and were kept in case they helped against the dragon, raising whether they were magical.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A single test with witch powder settled it.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Knowing whether they are magical is mainly practical.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Settled by a simple purchased reagent.

facts.text: Does the jeweled chalice Trout took from Sir Brandon's tomb belong to the church, as Brother Dirk suggests?

classification.grounding_justification: Brother Dirk's claim that tomb items are church relics raises the question of the chalice's ownership.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Ownership is a bounded fact one inquiry could settle.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly matters for whether the party must hand it over.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be checked with the church, little more.

facts.text: Dr. Uriah must give the barrow robes back to the church once the dragon is defeated, as he promised Brother Dirk.

classification.stake_basis: Brother Dirk insists the robes are holy relics belonging to the church and agreed to let Dr. Uriah keep them only until the dragon is defeated.

facts.text: Who does the noblewoman statue holding a stone sword in the Barrow Mound depict?

classification.grounding_justification: A prior Session established the statue as a notable, unexplained feature of the tomb, linked to the voice asking about true knighthood.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Identifying the figure is mostly an identification, though it may connect to the tomb's history.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Knowing who she is could illuminate the Barrow Mound's lore, but mainly fills in background.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be pursued through the church's tale of Sir Brandon or local lore, but no specific leads exist.

facts.text: Whose female voice spoke in the party's heads asking "What makes a true knight?" before the tomb doors opened?

classification.grounding_justification: A disembodied voice speaking telepathically before the doors opened is a conspicuous supernatural anomaly left unexplained.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal a hidden presence or intelligence tied to the tomb and its mechanism.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Learning the speaker would reveal a secret of the Barrow Mound and possibly reframe the knightly test.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be followed through the statue, the church's lore of Sir Brandon, or returning to the tomb.

facts.text: Cedric has signed a promissory note to pay the party for the barrow treasure, tallied by Dr. Uriah at 975 gold, payable once the caravans flow again.

classification.support_basis: The note is the party's means of paying Lady Hilda and Malzazarik, since Eric the Reeve may not pay in advance, but it pays out only once the caravans flow.

facts.text: Cedric's note cannot be paid until the caravans flow again, and his supplies have stopped since the dragon appeared.

classification.scope_basis: The note's payment is explicitly conditioned on the caravans flowing again, and Cedric's shipments have been stopped since the dragon troubles began, a continuing condition beyond the store scene.

facts.text: Is the magical ring Dunk took from the dead dwarf at the Dwarven mine cursed?

classification.grounding_justification: The beats explicitly state that whether the ring is cursed remains unknown, and Dunk put it on because he could not resist the urge.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Answering it confirms a property of the item rather than revealing a wider hidden situation.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: A curse would matter to Dunk, who is wearing it, but the answer is mainly practical.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: It could be settled by a check such as magical examination; little beyond that is suggested.

facts.text: How did Grimny die, and did his brother Bral kill him as Grimny's ghost believes?

classification.grounding_justification: Grimny's ghost explicitly accuses Bral, yet he did not know the mine had caved in and the cave-in looks natural, leaving the killing conspicuously unresolved.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal a hidden killing, its motive and its link to the cave-in and the burnt cabin.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: A brother murdering his kin for the hoard would be a substantial revelation tying into the map and the dragon.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: The cave-in, the burnt cabin, the dead dwarf and Bral himself offer leads to examine and question.

facts.text: What happened to the other dwarf brothers Grelli, Durney, Brenny, Tedry and Rooney?

classification.grounding_justification: Seven brothers worked the mine, but the cabin is burnt, the entrance caved in and a dead dwarf lies under the rubble, clearly raising their fate.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Their fate would reveal what happened at the mine beyond Grimny's death.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: It would explain the mine's ruin and possibly the extent of Bral's crime.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Digging through the cave-in and searching the mine plausibly yields leads.

facts.text: Where is Bral now?

classification.grounding_justification: Grimny names Bral as his killer and Bral's return from the faraway town leaves his current whereabouts open; Dunk speculates about him.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Locating him is largely a single discovery, though it may connect to the dragon suspicion.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly instrumental for confronting the suspected killer.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be pursued through leads about the hoard and the lair.
